Definition: bird of prey, usually thought to be the pelican (from casting itself into the sea)
BiblicalUsage: The pelican stands in the law's list of unclean birds, a bird of prey that casts itself into the sea. It appears twice, in Leviticus and in the repetition of Deuteronomy, in the same list of birds Israel was not to eat.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that even a pelican in a list of unclean birds shows God ordering every corner of His people's life, down to what dives into the sea.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
